purpose: Educate football fans on the historical evolution of the back-pass and goalkeeper time-wasting rules from the 1990 World Cup to the updated 2025 regulations.

sequences.name: Hook & Dilemma
sequences.pacing: Fast-paced motion collage contrasting modern restrictions with past allowances
sequences.role: Hook the viewer with dynamic visuals illustrating modern goalkeeper passing restrictions compared to ancient rules.

sequences.name: Show Title Card
sequences.pacing: Rhythmic branded identity sting with whistle audio
sequences.role: Introduce the series title 'Hikayat Qanun' (Story of a Law) centered on the back-pass rule.

sequences.name: The Catalyst: Italia 1990 & Egypt
sequences.pacing: Documentary archival montage with kinetic collage effects
sequences.role: Establish historical context: the dull Egypt vs Ireland 1990 match where keeper Ahmed Shobair repeatedly killed time via back-passes.

sequences.name: The 1992 Back-Pass Revolution
sequences.pacing: Technical infographic breakdown with 2D tactical pitch and player cutouts
sequences.role: Explain the 1992 FIFA back-pass ban, anatomical exceptions (head/chest allowed, feet forbidden), and indirect free-kick penalties.

sequences.name: The 1997 Six-Second Rule & Referee Dilemma
sequences.pacing: Mixed collage and vintage VHS clips with stopwatch kinetic typography
sequences.role: Show how keepers exploited the loop hole by holding the ball in hands, leading to the 1997 6-second rule and why referees neglected it.

sequences.name: The 2025 Modern Overhaul
sequences.pacing: Clean, punchy motion graphics and kinetic tactical diagrams
sequences.role: Reveal the new 2025 law: extending the time limit to 8 seconds and awarding a corner kick or throw-in to the opposing team.

signature_techniques.name: Halftone & Paper Cutout Collage on High-Contrast Pitch
signature_techniques.what: Isolating historical sports figures as black-and-white or high-contrast cutout silhouettes bordered by paper-edge mats over vibrant lime-green football pitch graphics.
signature_techniques.why: Bridges low-resolution vintage SD broadcast footage with crisp modern 9:16 mobile aesthetics, turning grainy archive material into stylish editorial graphics without quality jarringness- OBSERVED.

signature_techniques.name: Curved CRT Television Frame with Analog Scanline Accents
signature_techniques.what: Framing historical archival clips inside a curved barrel-distorted vignette mask with soft scanlines and timecodes.
signature_techniques.why: Instantly telegraphs historical flashbacks to the 1990s while preventing low-resolution horizontal broadcast clips from looking poorly cropped or stretched on 9:16 vertical displays- OBSERVED.

signature_techniques.name: Kinetic Infographic Law Explainer via Overhead 2D Pitch
signature_techniques.what: Translating abstract rule texts into animated overhead tactical diagrams using motion trails, neon dotted trajectories, and bold typographic labels.
signature_techniques.why: Enables immediate comprehension of complex spatial sports rules (back-pass angle, penalty box boundary, corner vs throw-in outcomes) within seconds- OBSERVED.

motion_philosophy: Perceived energy comes from snappy layer-separated pop entrances, tight audio-visual SFX synchronization, and rhythmic kinetic typography matching the voiceover cadence. Instead of sweeping continuous camera fly-throughs, the piece relies on rapid graphic hits, springy pop-ins, and layered parallax drifts that maintain viewer engagement on mobile vertical screens.
editing_philosophy: Rhythmic, modular sequence-based editing structured chronologically (1990 -> 1992 -> 1997 -> 2025). Edits alternate strategically between historical archival evidence and clean graphic explainers to balance authentic nostalgia with contemporary visual polish.
sound_philosophy: Precision foley and tactile UI sound effects (whistle blasts, marker doodles, analog stopwatch ticking, digital swooshes) synchronized down to individual word hits and graphic impacts, anchored under a clear, measured documentary voiceover.
storytelling: Problem-solution-dilemma-evolution narrative: Introduces the historical problem (time wasting in 1990), FIFA's first reform (1992 back-pass ban), the subsequent loophole (holding ball in hand), the flawed intermediate fix (1997 6-second rule), and the ultimate modern solution (2025 8-second rule with corner penalties).
visual_language: Bold chromatic pairing of deep Al Jazeera green, neon lime accents, and pure paper-white typography, accented by black-and-white halftone cutouts, vintage CRT framing, and tactical pitch iconography.
